terminal.profile.ros-environment.title: ROS 2 Environment
config.ROS2.env.distro.description: The ROS distribution to load (e.g. humble). Leave empty to use the environment default. Changing this re-collects the environment automatically.
config.ROS2.env.setupScript.description: Path to the ROS environment setup script (e.g. install/setup.bash). If empty: when pixiRoot is configured, its derived default script is used; otherwise a full path must be provided. Supports the ${workspaceFolder} variable. Changing this re-collects the environment automatically.
config.ROS2.env.pixiRoot.description: Root directory of the pixi environment. On Windows, leaving it empty falls back to c:\\pixi_ws; on non-Windows, empty means no derivation. Changing this re-collects the environment automatically.
config.ROS2.env.systemWatchFiles.descrip: Shell configuration files the environment collection depends on (e.g. ~/.bashrc); any change re-collects the environment. Supports ~ expansion and absolute paths. Changing this rebuilds the watchers from the new list automatically.
config.ROS2.env.allowEmptyWorkspace.desc: Empty-workspace inclination for the unified environment gate: when the workspace has no ROS 2 packages, allow gated features to proceed anyway — build task provider / empty builds (environment-side only) and IntelliSense generation (environment-side entries only). Default off. This never exempts the environment threshold: without a usable ROS 2 environment nothing runs or is written, regardless of this setting. Applies immediately.
config.ROS2.build.installLayout.enum.aut: Platform default: merged install on Windows, isolated install on Linux/macOS
config.ROS2.build.installLayout.enum.mer: Merged install (--merge-install): all packages share a single install/ prefix (recommended on Windows: avoids overly long environment variables with many packages)
config.ROS2.build.installLayout.enum.iso: Isolated install (each package gets its own install/<package>/ prefix; colcon default, no extra flags)
config.ROS2.build.installLayout.descript: Install layout: merged = all packages share a single install/ prefix; isolated = each package gets its own install/<package> prefix (colcon default); auto = merged on Windows, isolated on Linux/macOS. Freely combinable with the install method (installMethod). After switching layouts, delete install/ and rebuild (colcon refuses to mix layouts). Takes effect on the next build.
config.ROS2.build.template.description: Build command template (including the command name), split by shell lexing (spaces and quotes) before execution. Placeholders may be arranged, repeated or omitted freely: ${base_path} workspace root; ${packages_select} selected-packages segment (disappears entirely when nothing is selected); ${clean} auto-clean segment; ${install_method}/${install_layout} the two install axes; ${1}..${n} preset slots fed by the presets table (ROS2.build.presets); ${0} custom input. Unknown placeholders are kept as-is and logged. An empty template = build is rejected (empty command).
config.ROS2.build.presets.description:
Preset table feeding the ${1}..${n} slots of ROS2.build.template. Each key–value pair is one choice; two ways to write a pair:

- **"N|description"** (N = a number from 1) — a preset for slot ${N}. The value is the arguments inserted when checked (multiple arguments allowed; may reference ${0} and named arguments such as ${packages_select}). Several entries sharing one slot form mutually exclusive alternatives: all are listed in the picker; when several are checked only the first in written order applies. Slot numbers live in the keys, so adding/removing/reordering entries never shifts other slots.
- **A bare key** (no "digits|" prefix) — enables the "Custom input" entry (only when the template contains ${0}). The key is the caption above the input box; the value is the grey example inside it (empty = no example). With several bare keys only the first counts.

Notes: the first unescaped `|` separates a key — write `\|` for a literal pipe. Entries with a non-numeric slot (including 0), an empty description, or a non-string value are ignored. Deleting the whole setting restores the factory presets; an empty object means no presets. Changes apply on the next build.
config.ROS2.build.preflightWarnings.enum: Show none (checks and automatic fixes still run)
Silence only "silent no-op of method switching"; everything else still notifies
config.ROS2.build.preflightWarnings.desc: Notification mode for pre-build warnings (layout mismatch / install-method hard conflict / silent no-op of method switching). Checks always run; the automatic --cmake-clean-cache fix is unaffected. The "Don't ask again" button on the first silent-no-op notification writes this setting. Takes effect on the next build.
config.ROS2.build.installMethod.enum.aut: Auto (recommended): copy install on Windows, symlink install on Linux/macOS
config.ROS2.build.installMethod.enum.sym: Symlink install (--symlink-install): artifacts point back to the sources, so edits need no reinstall; on Windows requires Developer Mode or administrator rights
config.ROS2.build.installMethod.enum.cop: Copy install: artifacts are copied, no symlinks (colcon default behavior)
config.ROS2.build.installMethod.descript: Install method (three values aligned with the install layout installLayout: auto/symlink/copy). An explicit choice overrides the platform default; after switching, clearing install/ before rebuilding is recommended. Takes effect on the next build.
config.ROS2.tool.run.template.descriptio: Run command template (including the command name), split by shell lexing (spaces and quotes) before execution. Placeholders: ${pkg} package name; ${executable} executable name; ${0} run-arguments input box (pre-filled with this executable's last arguments; remove it to stop the prompt); ${1}..${n} preset slots fed by the presets table (ROS2.tool.run.presets).
config.ROS2.tool.run.presets.description: Preset table feeding the ${1}..${n} slots of ROS2.tool.run.template. Two kinds of keys: **a key without any separator** is the "Run arguments" input entry — the key itself is the description shown above the input box (only when the template uses ${0}), and its value is the grey example text inside the box (the factory default ships one; empty = no placeholder); with several such keys only the first counts. **A key "N|description"** (N = a number starting from 1) is a preset for slot ${N}: value = the argument segment applied when checked (multiple segments allowed). Entries sharing a slot number are mutually exclusive alternatives shown together; the first in written order applies. Once presets exist, the run dialog upgrades from an input box to a multi-select list; checkbox memory is keyed by package/executable. Only the first unescaped | splits a key (\| is a literal pipe). Keys with a non-numeric slot (including an explicit 0|), an empty description or a non-string value are ignored. Deleting the whole setting = factory presets; an empty object = no presets.
config.ROS2.tool.run.staleWarning.descri: Non-blocking warning toast on Ctrl+F10 run/launch when the installed copy is older than the source file - the run may not include your latest edits. The toast has a "Don't show again" button that turns this setting off. Turn this off yourself if you intentionally test older installs.
config.ROS2.tool.launch.template.descrip: Launch command template (including the command name), split by shell lexing (spaces and quotes) before execution. Placeholders: ${pkg} package name; ${launch_file} install-relative path within the package (nested subpaths preserved); ${launch_path} absolute install-side path; ${0} launch-arguments input box (pre-filled with this file's last arguments; remove it to stop the prompt); ${1}..${n} preset slots fed by the presets table (ROS2.tool.launch.presets).
config.ROS2.tool.launch.presets.descript: Preset table feeding the ${1}..${n} slots of ROS2.tool.launch.template. Two kinds of keys: **a key without any separator** is the "Launch arguments" input entry — the key itself is the description shown above the input box (only when the template uses ${0}), and its value is the grey example text inside the box (the factory default ships one; empty = no placeholder); with several such keys only the first counts. **A key "N|description"** (N = a number starting from 1) is a preset for slot ${N}: value = the argument segment applied when checked (multiple segments allowed). Entries sharing a slot number are mutually exclusive alternatives shown together; the first in written order applies. Once presets exist, the launch dialog upgrades from an input box to a multi-select list; checkbox memory is keyed by source file path (same-named launches in different packages stay separate). Only the first unescaped | splits a key (\| is a literal pipe). Keys with a non-numeric slot (including an explicit 0|), an empty description or a non-string value are ignored. Deleting the whole setting = factory presets; an empty object = no presets.
config.ROS2.tool.launch.yamlDefinitionEn: Go-to-definition in YAML launch files (F12, experimental): when off, no definition provider is registered for .launch.yaml at all (F12 gets no response from this extension), avoiding the definition indicator under string quotes; file-link underlines, hovers and completions are unaffected. Affects YAML only; XML and Python definitions are untouched. Applies after a window reload. Supersedes the former ROS2.launch.yamlNodeMatch setting.
config.ROS2.tool.doctorCommand.descripti: Full command string executed by the "Run ros2 doctor" command (split by spaces and quotes; the whole string is editable — append checks or output options). Applies on next execution.
config.ROS2.tool.rosdepCommand.descripti: Full command string executed by the "Install dependencies via rosdep" command (split by spaces and quotes; the whole string is editable — change the dependency path or append arguments). Applies on next execution.
config.ROS2.msg.systemRefreshMinutes.des: Refresh interval (minutes) for the rosmsg system message index; built-in types and workspace messages are unaffected. Applies immediately.
config.ROS2.msg.workspaceRescanMs.descri: Forced rescan period (milliseconds) for the rosmsg workspace message index, as a safety net for missed file events; 0 = disabled. Applies on the next cycle.
config.ROS2.msg.formatGradientStep.descr: Gradient step (characters) for rosmsg format column alignment: one tier per this length, each tier aligned to "longest type + 2 spaces". Larger values allow larger gaps. Applies on next format.
config.ROS2.msg.formatLineThreshold.desc: Single/double-line switch threshold (characters) for @optional annotations in rosmsg formatting: overly long merges split into two lines, short ones merge into one. Applies on next format.
config.ROS2.search.excludeFolders.descri: Additional folders excluded when scanning the workspace; affects package discovery, rosmsg/xacro workspace search and test discovery. Relative paths resolve against the workspace root; supports ${workspaceFolder}. This list is append-only: 11 built-in artifact/dependency directory names (build, install, log, logs, devel, node_modules, .git, .hg, .svn, dist, out) are always excluded and cannot be un-excluded — listing them here has no effect. Applies automatically (cache invalidates and rescans, about 5–10 s).
config.ROS2.search.followSymlinks.descri: Whether directory searches follow symbolic links. Off by default (prevents traversal blowups caused by symlinks such as shared mount points); when on, link targets become searchable but traversal may get significantly slower. Applies automatically (package-scan cache invalidates and rescans in about 5–10 s; other searches immediately).
config.ROS2.packages.refreshMs.descripti: Forced background rescan period (milliseconds) for the package list, 0 = disabled. Applies automatically (the background timer is re-armed with the new period).
config.ROS2.packages.userIndex.descripti: User-supplied package index for the dependency picker. Key = package name; value = "[py|]<description>" - the optional "py" prefix forces the [pure Python package] badge, and the description text replaces the row's description when the name matches a candidate. Entries that match nothing stay hidden. A pipe inside the description is escaped as "\|".
config.ROS2.ide.maintainPythonPaths.desc: Automatically maintain the two Python extraPaths keys in settings.json (python.autoComplete.extraPaths / python.analysis.extraPaths): on = the workspace ament_python package roots, install locations and environment-injected directories are added/removed and canonically ordered; off = fully manual — regenerating the IntelliSense configuration skips this side as well (reported as disabled in the feedback). Default on.
config.ROS2.ide.intellisenseEngine.descr: Engine for automatic maintenance of header search paths (include entries). Switching only stops maintenance on the target side; files left behind by the other side are not deleted. Applies when the IntelliSense configuration is regenerated next.
Auto-select by installed extensions: use the single one present; if both or neither are installed, maintain both sides
Maintain only the cpptools side: include entries in .vscode/c_cpp_properties.json are added/removed automatically
Maintain only the clangd side: include entries in .clangd are added/removed automatically
Disable automatic maintenance; manage include entries fully by hand
config.ROS2.ide.entryOverrides.clangd.de: Replacement table for entries generated into .clangd. Key = the exact Add token without the "- " list prefix (e.g. "-std=c++20", "-I/abs/path", "-isystem/abs/path"). Value = the replacement, used verbatim (a "-" prefix is never added automatically); an empty string removes the entry. Rules are chained to a fixed point, so A→B→C settles to C in a single sync; cycles drop the entry. Consumed only while the clangd side is being maintained.
Replacement table for includePath entries generated into .vscode/c_cpp_properties.json. Key = the exact entry string as written, keeping ${workspaceFolder} and any trailing "**". Value = the replacement, used verbatim; an empty string removes the entry. Rules are chained to a fixed point in a single sync; cycles drop the entry. Consumed only while the cpptools side is being maintained.
config.ROS2.ide.entryOverrides.python.de: Replacement table for directories generated into python.autoComplete.extraPaths and python.analysis.extraPaths (one table governs both lists). Key = the exact directory entry string. Value = the replacement, used verbatim; an empty string removes the entry. Rules are chained to a fixed point in a single sync; cycles drop the entry.
config.ROS2.ide.clangdTidy.description: Take over .clangd ordering: when enabled, each sync re-sorts managed entries into the canonical group order (flags, workspace -I, install -isystem, distro -isystem) and re-anchors the localized group comment lines; rows you added yourself keep their relative order at the end of the Add block. Default off - nothing is reordered unless you opt in. The effect is one-way: disabling it does not restore a previous order.
config.ROS2.ui.showWelcomeOnStartup.desc: Show the welcome page after the extension is installed or updated. The "Don't show again" button in the notification writes this setting. Applies on next launch.
config.ROS2.ui.showLeftovers.description: Show leftover entries in the Package Contents view: files that still exist under install/ but are no longer declared by the latest build (renamed/removed executables, commented-out setup.py entries). Hidden by default - toggle with the eye button in the view title bar.

config.ROS2.search.walkTimeout.message.t: Total walk budget in milliseconds for the rosmsg message index (whole-search deadline; when exceeded the scan stops and returns partial results). Keep clearly larger than the branch timeout. Changes apply to the next scan.
config.ROS2.search.walkTimeout.message.b: Per-directory branch budget in milliseconds for the rosmsg message index: one directory taking longer is truncated and the walk continues with its siblings; must be clearly smaller than the total timeout for branch truncation to mean anything. Changes apply to the next scan.
config.ROS2.search.walkTimeout.message.m: Maximum recursion depth for the rosmsg message index (0 = only the root folder's files). Changes apply to the next scan.
config.ROS2.search.walkTimeout.xacro.tot: Total walk budget in milliseconds for the xacro/urdf include graph (whole-search deadline; when exceeded the scan stops and returns partial results). Keep clearly larger than the branch timeout. Changes apply to the next scan.
config.ROS2.search.walkTimeout.xacro.bra: Per-directory branch budget in milliseconds for the xacro/urdf include graph: one directory taking longer is truncated and the walk continues with its siblings; must be clearly smaller than the total timeout for branch truncation to mean anything. Changes apply to the next scan.
config.ROS2.search.walkTimeout.xacro.max: Maximum recursion depth for the xacro/urdf include graph (0 = only the root folder's files). Changes apply to the next scan.
config.ROS2.search.walkTimeout.package.t: Total walk budget in milliseconds for the package-discovery scan (whole-search deadline; when exceeded the scan stops and returns partial results). Keep clearly larger than the branch timeout. Changes apply to the next scan.
config.ROS2.search.walkTimeout.package.b: Per-directory branch budget in milliseconds for the package-discovery scan: one directory taking longer is truncated and the walk continues with its siblings; must be clearly smaller than the total timeout for branch truncation to mean anything. Changes apply to the next scan.
config.ROS2.search.walkTimeout.package.m: Maximum recursion depth for the package-discovery scan (0 = only the root folder's files). Changes apply to the next scan.
config.ROS2.search.walkTimeout.test.tota: Total walk budget in milliseconds for the test discovery (whole-search deadline; when exceeded the scan stops and returns partial results). Keep clearly larger than the branch timeout. Changes apply to the next scan.
config.ROS2.search.walkTimeout.test.bran: Per-directory branch budget in milliseconds for the test discovery: one directory taking longer is truncated and the walk continues with its siblings; must be clearly smaller than the total timeout for branch truncation to mean anything. Changes apply to the next scan.
config.ROS2.search.walkTimeout.test.maxD: Maximum recursion depth for the test discovery (0 = only the root folder's files). Changes apply to the next scan.
